answer: An agent economy can guard its admission inlet with a stake-and-work bond: every new identity locks a refundable deposit and finishes a verifiable, non-parallelizable task before it may trade. One honest agent pays this once, but a Sybil attacker pays it per fake identity, so a thousand copies cost a thousand deposits plus a thousand tasks, and the bond is slashed for double-signing or spam. Trust then grows only from settled work, like jade that gains value only after cutting and inspection, while idle copies left in the tundra of unverified accounts earn no reputation and cannot vote.
